summary.text: Jaja of Opobo controlled the palm-oil trade of the Imo river and dealt directly with buyers in Britain, cutting out the coastal firms. In September 1887 the consul, Harry Johnston, invited him aboard a gunboat under a promise of safe conduct and seized him. Jaja was tried at Accra and exiled to St Vincent in the West Indies; allowed home in 1891, he died on the way.

routes.label: Jaja taken to Accra for trial
Exiled to St Vincent, in the West Indies

moments.title: Seized under safe conduct
moments.text: Jaja goes aboard to meet the consul and is not allowed to leave.

moments.title: Tried and exiled
moments.text: A tribunal at Accra sentences him to exile in the West Indies. He died in 1891 on the voyage home.
